text:
alex: Hey team — saw a canary OOM during long-seq benchmarks this morning. Heap grew steadily until OOM at ~6.3GB. Not obvious leak in our logs. Can anyone try a focused repro?
jiwon: Which canary and which commit? I can try to repro locally.
alex: Canary: canary-3, model-serving at commit 9b7f2a. Happened on a long-seq run (max_seq=4096) with kv-cache enabled. No spike in syscalls, memory looks like RSS creeping up.
tasha: Is this the same regression we've seen before with arena fragmentation after many rollouts?
ryan: Could be. Ask: are we observing anon mmap growth vs RSS due to jemalloc arenas? Can you grab /proc/<pid>/smaps and jemalloc stats when it starts growing?
alex: Good idea. CI has the canary PID 4127. I can dump smaps and jeprof later today. For quick checks, what commands do you want?
jiwon: Send smaps and /proc/<pid>/status. Also run:
```
cat /proc/4127/smaps > /tmp/smaps-4127.txt
curl -sS localhost:6060/debug/vars > /tmp/debugvars.json
# jemalloc stats via malloc_conf or API:
echo 'stats.print' | nc -U /var/run/jemalloc_4127.sock > /tmp/je.stats
```
ryan: And run heap profile snapshot (if enabled):
```
heaptrack --output=heaptrack.bin --pid 4127 --duration 60
# or gperftools: HEAPPROFILE=/tmp/heapprof /path/to/bin <args>
```
alex: CI run scheduled for 09:30 PT; I'll attach smaps + je.stats here after. If anyone can run a microbench with repeated short-lived allocations + long-lived caches that mimics kv-cache churn, that'd help isolate arena fragmentation.
tasha: I'll create a small reproducer that allocs 1-2MB slabs repeatedly and touches pages to avoid lazy commit. Will link PR.
ryan: If fragmentation, toggling MADV_DONTNEED on evicted pages might help — try running with --madvise-dontneed flag in runtime config and compare. Also test opt: malloc_conf=oversize_threshold:1,dirty_decay_ms:1000,muzzy_decay_ms:1000 to force faster purging.
alex: Noted. One more ask: if someone reproduces, please capture pmap -x and /proc/<pid>/numa_maps too. We suspect some persistent kernel page ownership.
jiwon: I'll run repro now on a dev node and paste logs. If it's quick I'll open a tiny issue and ping the allocator owners.
ci-bot: Canary canary-3 build 429 passed smoke, failed longseq (OOM). Logs: /ci/builds/429/longseq-failure.log
alex: Thanks — will upload artifacts shortly. If anyone sees a pattern (madvise effect, jemalloc stats showing retained arenas), reply here. :eyes:
ryan: If we get a reliable repro, we should try allocator patch to merge arenas on free or reduce per-thread arena count. Also try running with MALLOC_CONF:narenas:1 for a quick hypothesis test.
tasha: PR for reproducer: https://git.redwood.ai/rt/repro/merge-allocator-frag. Small test harness and instructions.
jiwon: Repro confirmed locally — RSS climbs ~200MB every 10 minutes under test. Dumping smaps/je.stats now and uploading.
alex: Awesome, upload links here and I'll file a postmortem ticket with initial triage. Thanks all. :pray:
